findings.title: Client deletion breaks with V2: listener calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled which throws UnsupportedOperationException
findings.body: The registerListener handler now runs whenever Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled (which V2 depends on). On ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent it calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients() now returns the new ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled() unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). As a result, deleting any client in a realm with the V2 feature enabled will propagate a RuntimeException from the event listener and fail the client removal (and leave the client-specific authorization resources orphaned). The V2 path needs a no-op/cleanup implementation for client removal, or the listener must skip the clients() call for V2.

findings.title: All-clients permission is ignored whenever a client-specific resource exists
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the all-clients ('Clients' resource type) fallback is only evaluated when resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), ...) returns null. If any client-specific resource exists for that client (e.g. another admin was granted a VIEW permission on that client, which creates the resource), the code evaluates only that resource's permissions and never considers permissions attached to the all-clients resource. An admin holding an all-clients MANAGE/VIEW/CONFIGURE permission would then be denied operations on that specific client, depending on which policies happen to reference the client-specific resource. Both the client-specific resource and the all-clients resource should be evaluated (granted if either matches), as in the V1 implementation where both the typed permission and the per-client permission are checked.

findings.title: Possible null resource passed to policy store when all-clients resource is missing
findings.body: When the client-specific resource is not found, the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately passes the result to authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource returns null when the resource is not found by name (e.g. realms where the admin-permissions resource server predates this change and was never re-initialized with the 'Clients' resource, since init() returns early when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null). Existing deployments upgrading to a version with this schema change will not have the 'Clients' resource/scopes created, so this can produce a NullPointerException (or store-specific failure) on every client permission check instead of a clean deny, and the new Clients scopes/resources are never provisioned for existing realms.

findings.title: Dead code: unused getEvaluationContext, logger and TOKEN_EXCHANGE import
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2 contains a private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) method that is never called (the only caller would be canExchangeTo, which now throws UnsupportedOperationException), plus an unused static logger field and an unused static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE. This dead code should be removed (or wired in when token exchange is implemented for V2) to avoid confusion about how token-exchange evaluation is supposed to work in V2.
